releases.displayName: "Suit Yourself!" Update Is Now Live - New Looks, Reworked Consumables & Quality

items.text: Hennessy has been on Sota7 for a while now. She has scanned hundreds of plants and befriended more animals than EON ever planned for. Now it's time to make her stay a little more comfortable.

The Suit Yourself Update is here, and it's all about doing things your way. New outfits and hairstyles, a new figurine to hunt down, a new quest for everyone who has finished the game, consumables that are actually worth cooking, labeled zones and regions on the map, Engineer settings you can change anytime, and a pile of quality-of-life improvements you've been asking for.
Suit up and let's dive in! ːhennesmileː
First up, something new to wear. We're adding 3 new outfits, 4 new hairstyles and 1 bracelet.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/dd3da06e356a6bb11b8812e3826108302716039a.gif"]
One of the new outfits is yours right away, no strings attached. The rest takes a little more effort, because EON doesn't just hand out fashion for free.

If you've finished the game, head out and look for the databoxes scattered across the map. That's where the other two outfits and the new hairstyles are waiting. Track them down, dress up, and finally give Hennessy's old jumpsuit a well-deserved rest.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/ad5a287c2ea86c0fd939775b416e7967605f38b4.gif"]
[table equalcells="1" colwidth=""]
⚠️ Important note: the bracelet isn't in a databox! It's lying somewhere out there on the map, so keep your eyes peeled during your next trip.
Found them all? Use a Mirror, open Photo Mode, strike a pose and share some photos of Hennessy in her new jumpsuit on our Discord. We want to see it!

[carousel autoadvance="true"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/9283711e571504403a6284bd86570413ca422564.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/042cf2d07e7a8a26078e6bfe8a5105e45b8cac82.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/82100eb6c7f79702bc32d0057db3b1a5699d51cf.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/8a240b3a6e7038e0253b6b1f4c281f521d5c3700.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/5da1e0e3e823d0e8c20f7c27e2c1990ff597d0d1.png"]

Until now, a crafted dish or drink mostly passed as a better version of the plants you made it from. Basically, you cooked, and the result was a slightly improved version of the ingredient in your hand.

But not anymore! We reworked 28 recipes, and every crafted dish and drink now gives noticeably more than the sum of its ingredients. Most of them also carry their own effects: positive, negative and neutral. Somnia Tea, for example, makes the local wildlife ignore you, but it also makes you tired faster. Cooking is a decision now, not a formality, and some recipes are worth the detour on their own. As a bonus, dishes now weigh half as much as before.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/548275aa1bd57d9c7d558b4b2d381a2c993743d2.gif"]

The panels around them were rebuilt to match. Effect rows no longer break after the first word, related effects sit together on one row, regeneration is shown as a percentage, instant effects no longer linger in the list as if they were still running, and the Engineer difficulty multiplier is visible right in the panel. All of the new effect texts are available in all 13 languages.
The map used to tell you where you were standing and very little else. Now it tells you precisely where you are.

Regions and biomes are now labeled, tribe locations are marked, and the areas that drain your immunity are drawn directly on the map, so you can see the dangerous grounds before you walk into them instead of after. Discovery fog and the map colors were reworked to go with all of it, which makes the map actually readable.

notes.title: ⚙️ Engineer Mode: Change Your Mind Anytime

items.text: Engineer mode lets you set your own rules. There was just one small problem. You had to set them all at the very start, and then live with your choices. Forever. Cranked up hunger and regretted it three hours later? Tough luck.

Not anymore! In Engineer mode, you can now change all of the mode's settings in-game, at any time. Turn hunger down, switch off aggressive animals, then crank everything back up when you're feeling brave. Suit yourself!
Options that leave a permanent mark on your world ask for a confirmation first, so you won't click something you didn't want to by accident.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/aceb4b0b4e76060093425a70801ef03bc16e90ce.gif"]
[p align="start"]Finally, a bunch of quality-of-life changes that should make everyday life on Sota7 a lot smoother.

Picking things up no longer leaves you with four half-empty piles of the same item. Items now stack together on their own, and they do it generously: two stacks with different durability merge and keep the better one. For the cases where that cannot happen automatically, for example after you split a stack by hand, there is an Auto Stack button in the inventory.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/421c3947709983c5975adc857a96786d2feca0c1.gif"]

Storage screens finally get two new buttons that do what the text on the button says. Take All empties a container into your inventory, Store All sends your haul the other way, and coming home from a long run stops being an entire minute of only clicking.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/4171cddbd982fbd99f026fa1eccbda3692a78cc2.gif"]

The Viper got a handling pass. We tuned its stiffness and the pull of gravity on it and polished how it reacts to what it rides over, so small plants and terrain edges no longer tip you off the board. That was one of the things you reported most often, so now getting around Sota7 should take a lot less staring at the ground in front of you.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/583e037aa0f865a07591c70380ebdb61a6988dfb.gif"]
That's not all! The update also brings plenty of smaller fixes and improvements. You'll find them all in the full changelog below.

A New Quest After the Ending: If you have finished the game, load the autosave the game makes just before the ending and a new quest starts on its own. The game tells you that this save is there if you want to keep playing. It works on saves you already have, as long as the game is finished on them.

New Outfits, Hairstyles and a Bracelet: Three new outfits, four new hairstyles and one bracelet. One outfit is available to everyone right away. The other two outfits and the hairstyles are hidden in databoxes scattered across the map and become available once you have finished the game. The bracelet is hidden somewhere on the map and can be found at any point in the game.
New Collectible Figurine: A new figurine is hidden somewhere on Sota7.

Crafted Food and Drinks: Dishes and drinks you craft now give noticeably more than the sum of their ingredients, and most of them come with their own positive, negative and neutral effects instead of copying the plant they are made from.
Lighter Dishes: Crafted dishes now weigh 350 g instead of 700 g.
Medicines: Medicines no longer spoil, and their action now reads "Consume" instead of "Eat".
Porridges: Porridges now spoil like other food.
Immunity Syringe: The immunity syringe no longer wears out after 3 days.
Gummy Sticks Recipe: The recipe now unlocks when you pick up its own ingredient, Viscous Secretion.
Immunity Preview: Immunity gains in the item preview are now shown as a percentage.

Effects Panel: Long effect rows wrap instead of breaking after the first word, the item preview keeps a steady height and only shrinks for long lists of effects, sub-effects of the same kind are paired on one row, time is shown as "/h" everywhere, and the Immunity stat name is translated. All new effect texts are available in 13 languages.

Status Screen: Effect rows no longer repeat their values, regeneration is shown as a percentage, instant effects are no longer listed as if they were still running, and the difficulty multiplier is shown in the panel.

Stat Preview Side Effects: Fixed the inventory stat preview changing your actual character. Carry weight no longer jumps between 80 and 110 kg or doubles permanently, animals no longer start ignoring you just because you previewed Somnia Tea, a preview can no longer damage you, and a previewed sleep dart no longer skips real game time.

Gameplay Settings During a Run: On Engineer difficulty you can now change gameplay settings mid-run from the settings panel, with a confirmation for options that leave a permanent mark on the world. This also fixes immunity starting to drain earlier than it should after a settings change, resetting to defaults not sticking and quietly switching your difficulty, crafts already in progress ignoring a new crafting speed, quick load bringing back old setting values, and the settings screen opening in the wrong place when you start an Engineer run.

Key Bindings Overhaul: Rebinding a key in one control context no longer affects the others, and conflicts are reported only between contexts that can be active at the same time. The controls screen now fully supports gamepad: separate bindings per device, button icons instead of key names, and a confirmation before a key is taken away from another action.
Mouse Wheel Binding: The mouse wheel can now be assigned to actions, and if you bind a key in its place, each press counts as one step.

Controls Screen Cleanup: Removed rows that did nothing (Open Last Window, Toggle Signal Manager, Toggle run/walk, Reload), merged the AR, map and vehicle rows, folded Scan into "Use item", moved the drone scan to the Drones section, and merged entering and leaving the scout drone with returning to your character into one row. Rotating the building tool with nothing selected switches the hotbar only when rotation is bound to the wheel.
Immunity Zones on the Map: Areas that drain immunity are now drawn on the map, together with region and biome names and tribe locations. Discovery fog and map colors were updated to match.

Auto Stack: Items you pick up now stack together in your inventory on their own, and they do it generously: two stacks with different durability merge and keep the better one. For the cases where that cannot happen automatically, for example after you split a stack by hand, there is an Auto Stack button in the inventory.
Weight Display: Your maximum carry weight updates right away after a buff, without reopening the inventory.
Take All and Store All: Storage screens now have Take All and Store All buttons, so moving a full load in or out of a container takes one click.
Encumbrance After Death: Movement restrictions from carried weight come back after the death screen instead of during it.

Baby Animals Can Be Petted Again: Babies can be petted at the same reputation as adults, stage 1 for Camilla and Lonebid and stage 2 for the rest. They stop fleeing as soon as an adult in their nest reaches that reputation, and petting babies is disabled during the taming tutorial. We also fixed where the petting interaction registers on baby Camilla, Lonebid and Zhalo.
Birds: Birds fly lower and closer to you now, and they are visible again after a rendering fix.
Automated Growpod: The automated growpod now harvests annual plants (herbs) as well.
Buggy Stuck in a Tree: Fixed being unable to leave the vehicle or use Unstuck when the buggy ends up hanging in a tree.
Hoverboard Tuning: Tuned the Viper's stiffness and the pull of gravity on it, so small plants and terrain edges no longer tip you off the board.

Dust Storm Never Triggered: If you picked up the Market memory core but the Dust Storm never started, the quest now starts automatically when you load or respawn, which unblocks The Door on saves you already have. We also added safeguards for Unstuck and for dying inside the Market.
Archivarium: The all-memory-cores achievement is now counted from the locks you actually filled, and granted when you load a save where you already did it.

Cartographer: The all-Igo-locations achievement counts a location as visited if you have been there or it is in your compendium, updates the moment you enter a location or unlock an entry, and is granted retroactively.
Hybrids: Hybrid achievements are re-checked every time a compendium entry unlocks.
Finished Game: If you have already finished the game, the achievements for it are granted when you load that save.
Location Triggers: The visit areas for the Hideout and the Stillheaven Meditation Center are larger now, so they register reliably.
Gate: Opening the big gate now unlocks its achievement.
Compendium Repair: Missing compendium entries are restored when you load your save, and the compendium keeps tracking your progress after the Studies achievement instead of stopping there.
If the Suit Yourself Update made your time on Sota7 a little better, please leave a review on Steam. It takes a minute, it helps us a ton, and it tells us what to work on next.

This patch is mostly about saves. Nests that came back empty, data boxes that reset themselves, map icons that disappeared and animals that vanished after an autosave all came from the same place, and the game now repairs that when you load your save. Thank you to everyone who sent us their save files, that is what made these fixes possible. Keep the reports coming if you spot anything else acting weird!
Empty Nests After Loading: Nests that came back empty after loading a save now rebuild their population automatically, so animals no longer disappear from a nest for good.

Lost Data Boxes: Data boxes you had already collected, but which a corrupted save had reset (for example a quest counter dropping from 23/24 back to 2/24), are restored when you load, based on the blueprints you unlocked.
Missing Map Icons: On saves that come up as corrupted, plant, animal and resource icons on the map are restored for every species already in your compendium.

Animals Lost During Autosave: Fixed animals that appeared or were removed while an autosave was running being left out of the save file, which made them disappear on the next load. We also fixed the underlying cause, where two objects could end up written over each other in the save.

Compendium Achievements: The fauna, flora and geology achievements are now decided by what is in your compendium. Saves where the tracking was never set up or was incomplete now grant the achievement when you load, as long as every required entry is known.
Nest Navigation: Fixed animal navigation around the Imperial Strider, Sage Strider and Nango nests.
Taming Actions: Added safety checks for animals that are removed while you are taming them or changing your reputation with them.

Another patch is out, and this one is mostly about achievements. The geology achievement was asking for a lot more than its name suggests, the hybrid ones could end up out of reach entirely, and new costumes stopped showing up in the garage mirror. All three are fixed, and all three are re-checked when you load a save you already have. Keep the reports coming if you spot anything else acting weird!

Geology Achievement: The geology achievement now asks only for soil samples and hard materials, instead of every environment and material entry in the compendium. Saves you already have are re-checked when you load them, so if you already meet the new requirement, the achievement is granted.

Xeno Zoologist & Costumes: Fixed new costumes for Hennessy no longer unlocking in the garage mirror once the Xeno Zoologist achievement had been earned. Registering a new animal always unlocks its costume.

Hybrid Achievements: The first animal hybrid, all animal hybrids and plant hybrid achievements are now granted when you load your save, based on the hybrids in your compendium. This repairs saves where they had become impossible to get.
Friendly Nests: Animals living in a nest where at least one animal is friendly toward you no longer turn protective or aggressive when you come close.
Dart Gun Auto Reload: Fixed the Dart Gun firing the wrong dart after it automatically loaded Sleep or Plant Booster darts.
Multiroom Collision: Fixed being able to walk underneath the multiroom.
Antenna Sounds: Antennas now have start-up, idle and shut-down sounds, and they fade out when the antenna is switched off or destroyed.
Safety Checks: Extra protection around vegetation hidden under buildings, the player marker on the map and the popup shown when you finish the game.

We're rolling out another quick patch! The Dust Storm quest fix that has been on our list for days is finally in, together with the repair for buildings you could not demolish. Thank you for your patience while we get everything back on track, and please keep the reports coming if you spot anything else acting weird!

Dust Storm Quest: Objectives now complete correctly if you collected the Memory Core before the Dust Storm quest was triggered. Saves you already have are checked when you load them, and steps you have already done are completed automatically.
Decrypting Lake's Mysteries: Fixed the quest not completing when the Mystery Core was already set in the wall. This is applied to existing saves as well, when you load them.

Sleeping Bag Repair: Buildings that could not be demolished because of the sleeping bag bug are repaired when you load your save, so you can take them down again. Sleeping bags now release the building only when you pick them up, so quitting the game or moving between levels no longer leaves a building stuck.
Hoverboard on Buildings: Getting off the hoverboard over a floor that is being demolished no longer leaves that building impossible to demolish.
Sleeping Bag Indoors: A sleeping bag placed inside a building now switches to indoor lighting right away instead of after a reload, and it loads correctly in multi-room buildings.

Arachnophobia Mode: Arachnophobia mode now replaces insects with rubber ducks. Switching the option in the Accessibility settings updates the insects already in the world right away, no reload needed.
Amber Land: Fixed a hole in the landscape.

Another update for you, improving the game step by step. This one is mostly for the completionists among you: the Compendium can be finished again, and the achievements that were stuck now unlock retroactively when you load your save. Thank you for sticking with us, and keep telling us when something is off.

Compendium Cleanup: Removed the entries that could never be unlocked (Hot Waters, Lead, Meteor Shard, Sapphire, Symbiolith). Saves you already have are cleaned up when you load them, so the Compendium can be completed.

Underground Deposits: Opening the boxes that unlock underground deposits now adds the Underground Deposits entry with full progress and re-checks the achievements tied to it, including for boxes you opened before.

Memory Core Achievement: The achievement for placing all Memory Cores in the Archivarium wall now unlocks when you place the last core, and it is granted on load if you already have them all in place.

Producer Range Rings: Range rings on producers (miners, silos and the like) now show only while you have something selected to build. Producers that are already built show a faded ring during placement, and the silo ring is no longer on screen all the time.

Nango Sounds: The Nango now has a full set of sounds: petting and scratches, eating, sleeping, resting, sitting, sniffing, getting scared, fainting and the rustle of its armour, plus reactions when it likes or dislikes something. Camilla's fainting and reaction sounds were updated as well.
Volcano Tunnel: Sealed the remaining openings in the volcano tunnel.
Sleeping Bag Repair: Buildings you cannot demolish because of the sleeping bag issue will be repaired when you load your save, and new ones will not get stuck that way.

Key Bindings Overhaul: Rebinding a key in one context no longer changes the others, and conflicts are only reported between contexts that can be active at the same time. The controls screen also gets proper gamepad support: separate bindings per device, button icons instead of names, and a confirmation before a key is taken away from another action.

Gameplay Settings During a Run: On Engineer you will be able to change gameplay settings mid-run, with a confirmation for the options that leave a permanent mark on the world. It also fixes settings that did not stick, difficulty quietly changing along with them, and immunity starting to drain earlier than it should.

Dust Storm Quest: Objectives complete correctly if you collect the Memory Core before the Dust Storm quest starts, and the same fix should unblock "Decrypting Lake's Mysteries". This one has been on the list for a few days now, it is turning out to be trickier than it looked.
Animal Reputation: We have started work on animals in nests reacting to the reputation you have with them. Early days, more when there is something to show.

We're still hard at work ironing things out based on your feedback and suggestions. We're immensely thankful for all of your support and activity on the forums and our Discord server. This game wouldn't be what it is without you all.

Item Durability Rate: A single difficulty setting now controls how fast everything you own wears out: tools you use, gear that drains while you wear it (gas mask, immunity pump, rebreather, light stick), the hoverboard, the drone, and food rotting in your inventory and in containers. Plants growing out in the world are not affected. The rate is 1.0 on Scientist, 1.25 on Survivalist and 2.0 on Space Hell, and the Engineer slider goes up to 2.0. On Scientist this makes wear consistent across all your equipment, where before a few items wore more slowly than the rest.
Fainting Penalty: Fainting now costs 5% durability on Scientist, 10% on Survivalist and 15% on Space Hell. Before it was 10% on every difficulty.
Storage Rotting: Every container and every inventory now slows rotting to 15% of the world rate, the same as your backpack always did. A powered fridge stops rotting completely.
Viper Durability: The Viper now lasts about one in-game day of use.
Construction Recipes: Buildings no longer ask for Diodes, so you will not be stopped by a material you have not unlocked yet.
Crafting Reach: Crafting stations now pull ingredients from lockers across a full-size room, not only from the ones standing right next to them.
Ingredient Cost & Refunds: Fixed ingredients being taken incorrectly when they were spread across several containers. Refunds now give back exactly what was used.
Zhalo Tracker: The Zhalo pointer fix from Hotfix #3 did not cover every case. The tracker now leads you to the Zhalo family correctly.
Critters on Detailed Terrain: Critters no longer occasionally sink into the ground.
Stability: Added safety checks around animal interactions, plants removed while they are still growing, and save loading.
Thorn Hazard: Fixed a thorn hazard floating above the ground.
Grim Garden: Fixed a rough spot in the terrain.
Amber Tree: Fixed collision on the medium amber tree.
Broken Vehicle Message: The "item broken" message now names the vehicle instead of showing an empty name.
Quest Text: Fixed a typo in a quest description.

Shadows: We moved shadow rendering to a more compatible method on every shadow quality level, which should remove the GPU crashes reported on some machines. Shadow range and quality were retuned along the way, and first person hands and held items cast shadows again.

These fixes are finished on our side, but they did not make it into today's build. We're sorry about that, and we know that for some of you one of them is the exact thing standing between you and getting on with your game. They are in testing now and go out tomorrow. We're patching as fast as we can without breaking something else on the way, and this batch needed the extra day.

Cave Passage: Players who left the cave through the entrance instead of the balcony could not get back inside, which blocked the Rumble. Once the Mystery Beacon is complete, the pedestal now offers an "Open the passage" prompt that opens the door without the figurine, and after the Rumble begins the door stays open. This works on saves you already have.

Nest Placement: Weeds, bushes and trees no longer block nest placement and are cleared under the nest once it is built. Nests tilt to follow gentle slopes. Spots that are too steep, too uneven, on a cliff edge or in water still tell you the structure does not reach the ground. Buildings such as the garage also clear grass and flowers under them, and you can no longer build on top of interactive plants.
Built Nests Produce Materials: Nests you build now give the same animal materials as the ones you find in the world.
Scout Drone Objective: "Discover an underground deposit" completes the moment the scout drone starts scanning, if you play with automatic resource discovery turned on.
Dust Storm Quest: Objectives complete correctly if you collect the Memory Core before the Dust Storm quest starts.

Compendium: Removed entries that could not be unlocked at all (Hot Waters, Lead, Meteor Shard, Sapphire, Symbiolith), so the Compendium and the achievement tied to it can be completed. Opening the box that reveals underground deposits now also unlocks that Compendium entry, including for players who opened it earlier.

New Quest - Second Life: After completing Miracle Season, a new quest asks you to build a Composter, feed it plant matter, and wait for it to produce biomass. Players who have already finished Miracle Season will receive the quest when they load their save.

items.text: First things first - sorry it’s been a little quiet from us lately! We swear it wasn’t intentional! So - again, sorry for going quiet, but we promise it was for a good reason! That reason being us pushing the whole game forward on every front - polishing, content, performance, you name it. And while we were at it, we got to work with some exciting new tech. It’s official: Honeycomb will be launching with Nvidia’s DLSS 4.5 and RTXDI! Take a look!

items.text: It’s been a few busy weeks here at our studio, and we’re thrilled to share a peek at how Honeycomb: The World Beyond has been evolving - so pull up a chair, settle in, and let us walk you through what’s been happening behind the scenes. Our team’s been juggling reworks, polishing systems, and breathing new life into assets you’ll soon get to experience yourselves.
If you'd prefer to watch a video version of this update, here's a video version of the entire devlog:
We’re introducing a completely new system - Immunity!

Sota7 is what it is - an alien planet. Therefore, its atmosphere contains certain pathogens that no space explorer from beyond can handle. EON-sealed structures, like your base, will remain your safe haven in-between expeditions, of course, a place where your Immunity won't be affected. But the moment you step outside? It's game-on.

Speaking of that - there is a way to stay safe and healthy outside, don’t worry! Hennessy will be equipped with the blueprint to craft Immunity Pumps, which you’ll be able to equip, increasing your Immunity, therefore giving you more time to explore.
We don’t want to show too much of this mechanic just yet, but here’s a peek at what the pump will look like!

One of our ongoing goals is making Sota7 easier to read and navigate without compromising exploration. Enter: the directional indicator.

It’s still very much a work in progress but we still wanted to show you the direction we’re heading in - literally. This feature is being added to help you orient yourself more intuitively, allowing you to react to danger or points of interest much quicker.

items.text: We’ve got some important news to share about Honeycomb: The World Beyond. After a lot of careful thought, we’ve decided to move the release window to the first quarter of 2026. We know that’s not what anyone wanted to hear, but it’s the right call for the game - we want to give ourselves the time needed to make sure Sota7 feels every bit as alive, rich, and captivating as we’ve imagined.

It’s been a long road, and we’re finally entering the polishing stage - that last stretch where everything starts to come together. Your patience and encouragement mean more than you know, and we’d like to show you a bit of what’s been happening behind the scenes.

Sota7 is evolving fast. The planet’s environments are getting their finishing touches - denser flora, new biomes, locations and subtle details that make every single one of them stand out. The goal is simple: to make every corner of the map feel distinct and worth exploring.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/94109e8c7cd1dfba7964a1add66a78cfc4a0b0ea.gif"]
And yes, the wildlife is growing too. The Nango is officially joining all the other fauna that make the world feel busy, unpredictable, and alive in small but meaningful ways.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/8d2a9a3a15d0409cb2504551ebba3fa58d59d114.gif"]

Survival on Sota7 isn’t just about nature - it’s also about the technology that keeps you going. The Drone Scout has been upgraded with a more robust second version, expanding its scanning range and usefulness in the field.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/59809c7f4de1fa7354010de7949c9a0b290a6132.gif"]
Meanwhile, the hoverboard has received some much-needed love, including new visual effects and improved animations that make gliding across the landscape smoother and more satisfying.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/d3ca02d6f6bbc3c2acb2ce7bc3eb639080700a52.gif"]

Even smaller quality-of-life tweaks are finding their way in - for example, underground deposits are now more visible and better integrated into the environment, making exploration more intuitive and rewarding.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/49c5a7c686c00db085d4c15431d5cccdfbbe7163.gif"]

Our animation pipeline has been busier than ever. Both Hennessy and the various crafting devices are getting brand-new animations to add fluidity and detail to how the world responds to you. It’s a quiet but crucial layer of polish that helps the game feel truly alive - the difference between something that moves, and something that simply exists.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/2e6def9cba3c782f94ce5c4760488ad745b4b0f4.gif"]

And for those of you who love sharing your adventures, Photomode is coming along beautifully. It’s evolving from a developer tool into a full-fledged creative playground, with poses, filters, lighting adjustments, and even stickers for the perfect cinematic or goofy shot. We’ve already been having a lot of fun with it internally.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/180f37dea09bae464c3c5a127e647df87052ce40.gif"]

Delays are never easy, but they give us what matters most - time to make Honeycomb: The World Beyond the experience it deserves to be. The progress we’ve made in the last few months has been tremendous, and the next steps are all about refinement and heart. If you want some even deeper insight into everything we've been working on so far, check out our stream as well.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39978845/475f347565b9603bbfbb2225ca635d6c87d1ba88.png"]
Stay safe, stay curious, and we’ll see you soon - out there, in the world beyond.
~ The Frozen Way Team

items.text: We’ve been silent for some time, but the work has been going strong for the past few months. But it all came down to this important message…
Please welcome our new Publishers with a round of applause!
We want to create something special and unique with our new friends at Snail Games USA. They’re the publishers of many incredible titles. But you probably know them most via ARK: Survival Evolved!
With that in mind, we would like to ask you for a bit more time to tie it all together before we publish a unique survival experience for you - our dearest players!
With the important stuff already out of the bag, let’s give you guys a quick development update.

To kick things off, we wanted to show you something really cool! Here's a video made by one of our testers, where we're building a base. Base building is one of the key features of the game, and we can't wait to see your own creations!
After your in-depth feedback about Hennessy, we decided to change her a bit.

Next on our agenda are a bunch of new critters that will make the world of Honeycomb: The World Beyond even more alive.

Our concept artists are also hard at work with new projects that we could bring into the game. Here are a few new projects they’ve finished drawing in the last few weeks.
Artificial Nest

Slime-like critters

In another quick peek, during the last beta test, we were able to gather a lot of feedback regarding the AR mode. From what we gathered, we decided to edit the effects to increase overall visibility within Sota7.

items.text: If you want to see our team once again: Here’s a little summary of PAX West we attended at the end of Summer:
Remember that Science is an art!
~Jacob and Honey Team
We're still at it and not stopping anytime soon! Yesterday we listed the changes that didn't make it into the build in time, and most of them are live right now. Please update your game and enjoy!

Nest Placement: Weeds, bushes and trees no longer block nest placement and are cleared away under the nest once it is built. Nests now tilt to follow gentle slopes, with the front resting on the ground. Placing on ground that is too steep or uneven, on a cliff edge or over water still shows "Structure does not reach the ground". Rocks, other structures, you and your drone still block placement.
Buildings Clear Vegetation: The garage and other buildings now clear grass and flowers under them, and you can no longer build on top of interactive plants.
Composter Collision: Fixed collision on the Composter.

Built Nests Produce Materials: Nests you build now produce animal materials, the same ones you get from the nests you find in the world (Camilla, Canul, Lonebid, Nango, Nibis, Strider, Wox, Zhalo, Zuma). Materials show up once the nest is built and animals have moved in, and you get more of them as more animals settle there.

Cave Passage: Players who left the cave through the entrance instead of the balcony could not get back inside, which blocked the Rumble. Once the Mystery Beacon is complete, the pedestal now offers an "Open the passage" prompt that opens the closed door without the figurine, and after the Rumble begins the door stays open. This works on saves you already have.
Scout Drone Objective: "Discover an underground deposit" now completes the moment the scout drone starts scanning, if you play with automatic resource discovery turned on.

Deleting the Active Profile: Deleting the profile you are currently playing on now moves you to another existing profile instead of leaving the game without one. Profile slots without a screenshot show a default image.
First Launch: Shader compilation no longer runs at the same time as the hardware benchmark on first launch, so the benchmark measures your machine correctly.
Polish Translation: Fixed the name of the objective for planting Amacure and Gemnox in one growpod.

Two things from yesterday's list are not in this build. The Dust Storm quest fix and the missing Compendium entries needed more than a day of work, and we would rather hold them than push half a fix into your saves. They are at the top of what is in testing right now.

Dust Storm Quest: Objectives complete correctly if you collect the Memory Core before the Dust Storm quest starts. The same fix should also unblock "Decrypting Lake's Mysteries" when the Mystery Core is already set in the wall.

Compendium & Achievements: The entries that could never be unlocked (Hot Waters, Lead, Meteor Shard, Sapphire, Symbiolith) will be removed, so the Compendium can be completed on saves you already have. Unlocks and achievements will also be re-checked when your save loads, including underground deposits and the Archivarium wall, so anything you have already earned will register once this update is out.
Key Bindings per Context: Rebinding a key on foot, in the drone or in a vehicle no longer changes the other two, and conflicts are only flagged within the same context, so you can reuse the same key.

Gameplay Settings During a Run: On Engineer you will be able to change gameplay settings mid-run, with a confirmation for the options that leave a permanent mark on the world. It also fixes settings that did not stick after a reset, difficulty quietly changing along with them, ongoing crafts ignoring a new crafting speed, quick load bringing back old values and immunity starting to drain earlier than it should.
Producer Range Rings: Range rings on producers show only while you have something selected to build, instead of all the time.

The Honeycomb demo is no longer available on Steam. Thank you to everyone who played it, sent us a bug report, argued with us about balance or simply told a friend about a game they had never heard of. A lot of what is in the full version exists because of you.

The demo is a pre-release build, and it falls further behind with every hotfix we ship. We don't want anyone's first hours on Sota7 to be a version without the crash fixes, the new guides, the Composter and everything else from the past week. Keeping it up also means testing and shipping every change twice, and right now every hour we have goes into the released game: fixing what you report, filling out content and preparing the next updates.
For a lot of you this is not goodbye at all. You are on our Discord and in the forums, and your reports are in the patch notes above. Thank you for that.
Our friend, Alidove, was super kind to make a dedicated guide for the game!
So if any of you ever feel lost or need some help, their video is a true lifesaver. Thank you Alidove for the amazing guide!

The Earth as you know it has ceased to exist. The Eco-Apocalypse is here and now. The once vibrant animal kingdom, lush forests, vast seas and oceans have been lost in the abyss of nothingness. The natural resources from which we drew so much are gone irreversibly. Forced by unfavorable conditions on the surface, people moved to underground cities, leaving behind the splendor of the sun and the beauty of the blue sky. Now, only a sizable ozone hole yawns above their heads, showing the scale of the changes that have taken place on our planet.

Years have passed and science has reached the edge of its capabilities. After many attempts, the mighty heads have mobilized the nobles of this world to undertake a risky experiment. This project is the last salvation for the planet, as well as for human development itself.

Out of many, the daredevils were chosen. Training in preparation for the expedition was exhausting and stressful, but it was successful. Finally, we can say it: it's time to explore the unknown world!
The long flight was not one of the most pleasant, but Hennessy arrived at her destination. Here is where the adventure begins, explorer. Dive into the new world and rush towards the unknown.
Sup, Explorers!

notes.title: Welcome to the first ever development update of Honeycomb!

items.text: In this development update, we'd like to show you some cool concept arts that we've already prepared. Additionally, we'll explain a little bit why the development is taking so long. Last but not least, we'll showcase you some really great animations and a little sneak peek of what you can expect from the upcoming update. This time has been busy for us, but now we want to share a little piece of our creation. Adventure into the unknown begins now, explorer. Don't hesitate and dive into the marvelous world of Honeycomb.

We know it's been a long time since we announced Honeycomb, so it's time to bring you some answers. As a bioengineer, you get to experience a vibrant and colorful world. It's all about feeling free and being able to uncover this untouched land as you wish. There are a lot of things to pay attention to, so keep your eyes open if you don't want to miss the clues! We also want to share that special feeling of what it's like to be a real scientist. That's why we’re composing such a complex ecosystem to evoke a sense of authenticity in you.

To better introduce you to the theme of our game, we'd like to mention the term – crossbreeding. It works on the principle of a Taxonomic tree, so it is important to remember that it is impossible to combine incompatible species from different families. You will study how and which elements of flora and fauna will give the expected combinations. Furthermore, we’ll give you many opportunities to genetically crossbreed those plants.
In addition, here you have some ideas of underground fruits. You can expect different textures, which we’re working on.

When it comes to crossbreeding of animals, the case is a little different from plants. We won't play with their genes, because we're concerned about ensuring that they're not harmed. That's why crossbreeding occurs naturally, by animals pairing up with each other in the wild. However, there is also your role in the whole process.
What is more, we’ve been working on the tail physics. Check it out below and let us know what you think of it?

As you can see, we've prepared some ideas for creatures and plants already, and many more are yet to come. But we don’t stop here – it’s time to present to you another stuff we’re constantly working on. Say hello to the amphibian animal.
We think it looks cool and majestic, but a little clumsy. Just look at this cute tongue sticking outside its mouth. So adorable!
If you have dulled your eyes with the appearance of our creature, you may also like the animation of its movement, which we’re constantly improving.
We don't want to keep you in suspense, so we’d like to add a heartening piece of news at the end. The next devlog is already in the making, and you can expect it soon.
We also have a little surprise for you. Try to guess what it is and let us know in the comments section below.

We hope that you liked our little concept showcase. As we've mentioned earlier in this development update, from now on you can expect regular updates from our side. Once again, thank you for your patience. Share your opinions in the comments, and see you next time!
And last but not least, you can add Honeycomb to your wishlist, as well as follow the game, if you want to stay up-to-date with any news:
It's time to leave the cradle, explorer!
Team Honey~
